gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-tc: Noto Sans TC takes tall, wide-mouthed letters and lets its curves open outward rather than curl back in, a plain sans through and through. College above it stays bold and uniform, so lines run smoothly.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Wire-bent and constant in thickness, College looks like a shop sign. Noto Sans Telugu sits beneath with a high midline and open counters, giving the sign-like headline a quieter, more connected line of text to hand off to.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-thai: Rounded and puffed up like glass beads, this body text reads soft and welcoming. Noto Sans Thai handles the quiet, inviting work in a paragraph, while College draws its ruler-and-compass lines for the loud, authoritative opening.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-thai-loo: Noto Sans Thai Looped has tall bodies that make its lowercase look bold, with spacious gaps where the curves finish. Noto Sans Thai Looped keeps a paragraph feeling sturdy yet open, while College's marker-like line sits steadily above it.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-tifinagh: Noto Sans Tifinagh keeps its rounded letters open and inviting, with bowls that swell to fill the line. And College, drawn in one monoweight stroke, handles the headline, so a slightly larger size for it makes sense.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Contemporary in feel, College runs its diagonals to match its stems and fills every counter generously. Noto Sans Tirhuta joins it with cut-back terminals and a dominant x-height, and that sharp, open contrast is the pair's best trait.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Noto Sans Ugaritic keeps its x-height almost level with the caps and leaves its letter mouths open like unjoined chalk arcs. College is best at headlines, with joints that meet without thinning or bulging, but the body face handles paragraphs.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-vai: Letters bent from one single length of wire give College its signature look. And Noto Sans Vai backs it up with a modern, approachable body whose words read as solid blocks, with generous space where curves leave the stem.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-vithkuqi: Noto Sans Vithkuqi reads clean and modern, with open throats on its a, c, e and s. College supplies stems and arches of identical thickness above it, so headline and text feel built by the same hand.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Hulking and chalky, this lowercase looks pressed down hard, with a wide gap at the e's terminal. Noto Sans Wancho keeps a long page feeling solid and contemporary, while College holds its constant stroke width above it.
